key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene chemistry in MAPbI3 precursor inks depends strongly on the iodide-containing component: I2/polyiodides rapidly degrade it, PbI2 oxidizes it more slowly, and MAI helps stabilize the surface.
engineering_relevance: MXene incorporation into halide perovskite devices must be designed around precursor chemistry and mixing order to avoid flake degradation and to tune interfacial performance.
method: X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) to track MXene surface chemistry changes
Density Functional Theory (DFT) to explain adsorption and oxidation mechanisms
Component-wise exposure to MAPbI3 precursor species and their combinations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a combined XPS/DFT study showing distinct, component-specific oxidation and adsorption pathways, including rapid degradation by I2/In− and stabilization by MAI.
watch_item: The precursor addition sequence can alter the MXene surface state, so processing order is a critical implementation variable.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
